steps.body: Every number lives on a street between two tens — its **neighbors**. 47 lives between 40 and 50. Rounding to the nearest ten just means naming the CLOSER neighbor: 47 is 7 steps from 40 but only 3 steps from 50, so 47 rounds to 50.
Walk to the closer neighbor yourself.

widget.prompt: 47 lives between two tens. Slide the marker to the neighbor that is CLOSER to 47.
widget.lowFeedback: That ten is far below 47 — its two neighbors are the tens right beside it. Which is fewer steps away?
widget.highFeedback: You've slid past both of 47's neighbors. Come back toward the tens on either side of 47.
widget.successFeedback: 50 it is — only 3 steps from 47, while 40 sits 7 steps away. The closer neighbor wins.

predict.prompt: Before you slide: which ten is closer to 47?
predict.reveal: 47 sits 7 steps from 40 but only 3 from 50 — the closer neighbor wins, and the slider will show it.

steps.body: The shortcut: look at the **ones digit**. Ones of 1–4 mean the lower ten is closer (round down); ones of 6–9 mean the higher ten is closer (round up). It's not a new rule — it's the step-counting, compressed into one glance. (The 5 gets its own lesson soon.)
One glance at the ones digit.
explanationVariants: 63's ones digit is 3 — in the 1–4 club — so the lower ten wins: 60.
Count the steps: 63 is 3 from 60 but 7 from 70. Closer neighbor: 60.

commonPlacements.feedback: 70 is the FARTHER neighbor — 63 sits just 3 steps from 60 but 7 steps from 70. Ones digits 1–4 round down.
65 is the street's halfway mark, not a ten. Rounding lands on a neighbor — a number ending in 0.

steps.body: Everyone on the 30-to-40 street, go home.

widget.prompt: Round each number to its nearest ten.

items.feedback: 34 is 4 steps from 30 and 6 from 40 — the lower ten is closer.
36 is 6 steps past 30 but only 4 short of 40 — up it goes.
31 barely left 30 — just 1 step away. Easiest round on the street.
38 is only 2 steps from 40 — nearly there already.

widget.missFeedback: Check each ones digit: 1–4 go home to 30; 6–9 go up to 40.
widget.successFeedback: All home: 34 and 31 down to 30; 36 and 38 up to 40. The ones digit called it every time.

steps.body: What does a rounded number actually MEAN?
explanationVariants: Rounding names the nearest landmark: 30 is the ten closest to 27, three steps away.
27 doesn't change — we're just describing it by its closest ten for quick thinking.

widget.prompt: Rounding 27 to the nearest ten gives 30. What does that mean?

options.label: 30 is the ten closest to 27 — just 3 steps away
options.feedback: Rounding is a nearest-landmark report. 27 keeps being 27; 30 is its closest ten.

options.label: 27 has now become 30
options.feedback: 27 never changes! Rounding describes it by its nearest ten — a nickname for quick math, not a makeover.

options.label: 27 was wrong and 30 is the correction
options.feedback: Nothing was wrong — 27 is exact. Rounding trades a little exactness for a lot of speed, on purpose.

options.label: Any number ending in 7 gets 3 added
options.feedback: Adding 3 is what happened to LAND on the neighbor, not a rule about 7s. The real rule: name the closer ten.

steps.body: One more round-and-add warm-up before the two jars.
explanationVariants: 22 rounds down to 20 (ones digit 2); 17 rounds up to 20 (ones digit 7). Add the rounded pair: 20 + 20 = 40.
Two separate rounds first — 22→20 and 17→20 — then one easy addition of tens: 40.

widget.prompt: Round 22 to its nearest ten, round 17 to its nearest ten, then add the two rounded numbers. What do you get?

commonErrors.feedback: 39 is the EXACT sum — round each number first: 22→20, 17→20, then add: 20+20=40.
22's ones digit is 2 — in the round-DOWN club (0–4) — so it stays at 20, not up to 30. 20+20=40.
17's ones digit is 7 — in the round-UP club (5–9) — so it climbs to 20, not down to 10. 20+20=40.

explanationVariants: Round each player first, then compute the friendly version: 50 + 30 = 80 (the exact 78 sits right beside it).

widget.prompt: One jar holds 47 marbles, another holds 31. Round EACH to its nearest ten, then add the rounded numbers. What estimate do you get?

commonErrors.feedback: 78 is the EXACT sum — good arithmetic, wrong game! The estimate adds the rounded jars: 50 + 30.
70 rounded 47 DOWN to 40 — but 47's ones digit is 7, so it climbs to 50.
90 rounded 31 UP to 40 — but 31 is just 1 step past 30. Its ones digit 1 keeps it down.

steps.body: You can find any number's closest ten.
takeaways: Every number lives between two ten-neighbors; rounding names the closer one.
Ones digit 1–4 → down; 6–9 → up. It's step-counting in one glance.
Rounding doesn't change a number — it nicknames it for fast math.

concept.body: Quick rewind. Draw the street: 40 —— 47 —— 50. Count steps each way: 7 back to 40, 3 forward to 50. **Fewer steps wins.** That's all rounding is — finding which ten-neighbor takes the shorter walk.

explanationVariants: 52 is 2 steps from 50 and 8 from 60 — the short walk goes to 50.
Ones digit 2 is in the 1–4 club: round down.

options.feedback: Just 2 steps away — the closer neighbor by far.
60 is 8 steps from 52 — the long walk. The ones digit 2 points down the street to 50.
